accept.title: Contraste
items: accept = say yes to an offer, condition or responsibility, or receive something willingly
agree needs its own pattern: agree with someone, agree on a decision, agree to a proposal

achieve.title: Contraste
items: achieve + goal/result/success = accomplish something, often through effort
reach + place/point/level/decision/agreement = arrive at an endpoint

adjust.title: Contraste
items: adjust something = make a small practical change to improve fit, function or accuracy
adjust to something = become comfortable with new conditions
adapt to something = change behavior or method more broadly to suit a new situation

affect.title: Contraste
items: affect = usually a verb: influence or change something
effect = usually a noun: the result or consequence
effect can also be a formal verb meaning bring about, as in effect change

allow.title: Contraste
items: allow someone to do = neutral and works in passive forms: We were allowed to leave
let someone do = more conversational and uses the verb without to: They let us leave
For permission in the passive, use be allowed to, not be let to

answer.title: Contraste
items: answer + question/call/email takes the object directly
respond to + question/comment/request uses to and is often slightly more formal
A response can be a reaction; an answer usually addresses the question or message directly

attend.title: Contraste
items: attend + meeting/class/event = be present at it
assist + person = help someone; it is not the normal English equivalent of Portuguese assistir

cause.title: Contraste
items: cause someone to do = neutral or formal and focuses on the result: The delay caused us to miss the flight
make someone do = more direct and uses no to before the verb: They made us wait

control.title: Contraste
items: control = directly determine or limit behavior, access, movement or level
manage = organize, run or handle something; it does not necessarily mean having full control
manage to + verb = succeed in doing something, a separate meaning

convince.title: Contraste
items: convince often focuses on changing what someone believes or accepts as true
persuade often focuses on influencing someone to take an action
The verbs overlap in some contexts, especially before someone to + verb

cost.title: Contraste
items: Something costs an amount; a person spends an amount on something
cost can also mean cause a loss: The mistake cost us time
spend also works with time: spend two hours on something / doing something

discover.title: Contraste
items: discover = become aware of something previously unknown, sometimes unexpectedly
find = locate something or reach an answer/solution
find out = learn information, often after asking, checking or investigating

discuss.title: Contraste
items: talk about + topic is more conversational and uses about
discuss often suggests a more focused exchange of ideas, options or problems

do.title: Contraste
items: do commonly goes with tasks, work and activities: do research, do the work, do your best
make commonly goes with creating, producing or causing a result: make a plan, make a decision, make a mistake
Many do/make combinations are fixed collocations, so meaning alone does not always predict the verb

encourage.title: Contraste
items: encourage someone to do = support, motivate or give confidence to take an action
persuade someone to do = try to change their decision so they take the action
encourage does not imply that the person was initially unwilling

get.title: Contraste
items: get is a broad conversational verb that can mean receive, obtain, become, arrive or understand, among other uses
obtain specifically means acquire or secure something and is more formal
obtain works with things such as permission, information or approval, but it cannot replace get in get tired, get home or get it

have.title: Contraste
items: have + noun expresses possession, experience or a relationship: have a car, have a problem, have a meeting
there is/are introduces existence or presence: There is a problem
Portuguese tem may correspond to have or there is/are depending on whether someone has it or it simply exists

hire.title: Contraste
items: hire = employ a person or pay a professional to do work
rent = pay to use a car, apartment or equipment temporarily
In American English, rent a car is standard; hire a car is mainly British English

know.title: Contraste
items: know someone = be familiar or acquainted with that person
meet someone = encounter or be introduced to that person, often for the first time
get to know someone = become familiar with the person over time

lend.title: Contraste
items: lend = give something temporarily; the subject is the giver
borrow = receive something temporarily; the subject is the receiver
lend something to someone / borrow something from someone

let.title: Contraste
items: let someone do uses the verb without to
allow someone to do uses to and is often more neutral or formal
For passive permission, use be allowed to rather than be let to

make.title: Contraste
items: make commonly goes with creating, producing or causing a result: make a plan, make progress, make a mistake
do commonly goes with tasks, work and activities: do research, do the work, do your best
Many make/do combinations are fixed collocations, so meaning alone does not always predict the verb

manage.title: Contraste
items: manage to do = actually succeed in doing something, often despite difficulty
can/could = express ability or possibility and do not by themselves say that the action was completed
In a specific past situation, managed to often makes the successful outcome explicit

need.title: Contraste
items: need to and have to can both express necessity and often overlap
have to often presents a requirement or circumstance; need to often focuses on what is necessary, but this is a tendency rather than a strict rule
don't have to and don't need to mean there is no necessity; mustn't expresses prohibition

offer.title: Contraste
items: offer something = make it available for someone to accept
offer to do = volunteer to perform an action
suggest something / suggest doing = propose an idea or course of action rather than make something available

order.title: Contraste
items: order food/drink = request it as a customer from a menu or service
ask for something = make a general request and does not necessarily involve buying or placing an order
order someone to do = command someone to perform an action

produce.title: Contraste
items: produce = create or generate an output, result or goods
make = broader everyday verb for creating, preparing or causing something
manufacture = produce goods through an industrial process

realize.title: Contraste
items: realize = become mentally aware of or understand something
notice = become aware through seeing, hearing or paying attention
realize often introduces a new understanding; notice often starts from something observed

say.title: Contraste
items: say focuses on the words or message; the person is usually introduced with to
tell is normally followed directly by the person receiving the information
say something to someone / tell someone something

see.title: Contraste
items: see = perceive visually, often without deliberate effort, or understand something
look at = deliberately direct your eyes toward something
watch = keep looking at something over a period, especially movement, activity or change

suggest.title: Contraste
items: suggest doing = propose an activity: I suggest waiting
suggest that someone do = standard American English pattern: I suggest that he wait
suggest someone to do and suggest to do are generally not used for this meaning

tell.title: Contraste
items: tell is normally followed directly by the person receiving the information
say focuses on the words or message; use say something to someone when naming the listener
tell someone something / say something to someone

watch.title: Contraste
items: watch = keep looking at something over a period, especially movement, activity or change
look at = deliberately direct your eyes toward something
see = perceive something visually, often without deliberate effort

win.title: Contraste
items: win + game/match/competition/prize = be successful in the event or receive the prize
beat + person/team/opponent = defeat the other side
We won the game / We beat them
